mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the federal funds rate above 4% over the prior month reduces the discount rate applied to expected future earnings, lowering the present value of future cash flows and thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns in the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by 0.5% in the prior month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive despite FEDFUNDS increase, or IC > 0.05 over the 20-day horizon.

mechanism_narrative: Rising employment momentum as measured by PAYEMS exceeds 10,000 monthly increases while UNRATE remains below 6%, signaling labor market strength that boosts investor confidence and drives S&P 500 gains over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: IC < 0.05 over the 60-day horizon or 60-day returns are not statistically different from zero (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in consumer demand proxies like HOUST (units) coinciding with a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) creates a contrarian signal; S&P 500 forward returns turn negative over the next 5 days when this pattern persists.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by >15% while INDPRO decreases by >5% in the prior month
failure_condition: 20-day IC > 0.1 or 5-day returns are positive when the pattern occurs.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained contraction in manufacturing output (INDPRO < 105) persists for three consecutive months while GDP deflator inflation (CPIAUCSL) remains below 2%, indicating supply-side easing that supports equity valuations and produces positive 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: IC > 0.1 over 20 days or returns are negative despite the supply conditions.

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS remains above 4.25% for two consecutive months in a low-inflation regime (CPIAUCSL < 260), the higher real interest rate path suppresses growth expectations and yields negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are positive despite high FEDFUNDS and low CPIAUCSL.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden spike in job openings (RSAFS > 500K) followed by a decline in unemployment (UNRATE < 4.5%) creates a labor market tightening signal that drives positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS increases by >200K and UNRATE falls below 4.5%
failure_condition: IC > 0.1 over 60 days or returns flat with no mean reversion.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive monthly declines in consumer confidence proxies (not available in the catalog) are replaced here by a pattern of declining retail sales momentum (PAYEMS < 120K) while industrial production (INDPRO) remains flat, signaling a demand softening that predicts negative 5-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS decreases by >10% while INDPRO remains within ±2% of prior month

mechanism_narrative: During a regime shift to monetary tightening (FEDFUNDS crosses above 5%), S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days tend to be negative regardless of other macro variables, indicating a regime-dependent risk premium.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are positive or regime condition not confirmed by FEDFUNDS crossing.
